approachQuestion.prompt:
Parcel Lanes

A mutable array lane contains only the integers 0, 1, and 2, denoting three parcel classes. Rearrange it into all zeroes, then all ones, then all twos. Preserve multiplicities. Relative order among equal entries is irrelevant; do not resize the array. Return lane itself.

Constraints: 0 <= n = lane.length <= 200000.

Example 1: lane=[2,0,1,2,0,1] -> [0,0,1,1,2,2].
Example 2: lane=[2,2] -> [2,2].
Example 3: lane=[] -> [].
constraints: Choose the most efficient valid approach for the entire stated input domain; accept equivalent optimal variants.

options.text: Maintain low=mid=0 and high=n-1. While mid<=high: on 0 swap mid with low and increment both; on 1 increment mid; on 2 swap mid with high and decrement only high.
options.feedback: The swap from the right imports an unclassified entry, so mid must remain until that entry is inspected. The unknown region shrinks every iteration.

options.text: Count each of 0,1,2, then overwrite the input with exactly that many zeroes, ones, and twos.
options.feedback: Only class multiplicities matter; three counters retain all information needed to produce the required array with fixed storage.

options.text: Copy each class into a separate buffer and write the buffers back in class order.
options.feedback: It is correct but retains every entry unnecessarily when swaps or three counters suffice.

options.text: Use low, mid, and high as in the region method, but increment mid as well as decrementing high after every swap of a 2 to the right.
options.feedback: For [1,2,0], the right swap produces [1,0,2] and skips the imported 0, leaving the wrong order.

feedback.reason: Maintain classified outer regions and an unexamined middle; re-examine entries swapped in from the unexamined right boundary.
details: Use low and mid at the beginning and high at the end. Keep zeroes before low, ones from low through mid-1, and twos after high. On zero swap with low and advance both low and mid; on one advance mid; on two swap with high and decrease high without advancing mid.

After swapping a two with high, the newly arrived middle value is still unknown and must be inspected. Advancing mid unconditionally would skip it. The invariant separates zero, one, unknown, and two regions.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method revealed after question 1, choose its tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed access and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include all temporary buffers, input copies, and call frames; exclude supplied input and returned output. n is input length. Supplied lane is also output. No input copy, hashing, amortization, or recursive call stack is used.
constraints: Analyze this fixed method regardless of your answer to question 1; choose the tightest pair.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Every iteration shrinks the unknown region by one position.
details: Every iteration shortens the unknown region [mid,high] by one, so there are exactly n iterations. A fixed number of indices and a swap temporary are stored; no recursion or work arrays occur.

Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed access and signed 64-bit arithmetic. No input copy, hashing, amortization, or recursive call stack is used.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This adds an input-sized buffer absent from the fixed method.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This counts repeated full scans that the fixed method does not perform.
“O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The fixed method does not perform sorting or independent binary searches.
